title: Crystal structure and photo- and electroluminescent properties of a “sandglass” terbium cluster

synthesis.procedure: The complex was prepared by mixing hpmba (4.0 mmol) with the corresponding lanthanide perchlorate (2.25 mmol) in 10 mL of ethyl acetate, with the pH adjusted to ca. 7 using triethylamine. Triprism crystals formed after several days of standing at room temperature (yield 16%).
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Triprism crystals appeared after several days depositing at room temperature.

properties.summary: Compound 1 is strongly green-emissive from Tb(III). In acetonitrile at 298 K, excitation at ~300 nm gives 5D4→7FJ bands at ca. 487, 546, 583 and 622 nm with a 5D4 lifetime of 1.03 ms at 546 nm (abstract: ~1.02 ms); ligand emission at 441 nm is fully quenched. In mixed CH3CN solutions, adjusting pH to ca. 7 with triethylamine enhances Tb emission by ca. 17 times relative to ligand/Tb(ClO4)3 mixtures. An ITO/PVK/complex/Al OLED shows voltage-dependent electroluminescence matching the PL spectrum (max. 546 nm; weaker 487, 583, 622 nm), with maximum EL intensity at 11 V.

measurements.conditions: CH3CN; 4.00×10^-4 M hpmba + 2.25×10^-4 M Tb(ClO4)3, pH adjusted to ca. 7 with triethylamine
